metadata.title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire

analysis.themes: A painter hired to secretly portrait a reluctant bride falls in love with her subject — the film treats looking itself as the first act of love and memory as the last.
analysis.atmosphere: Hushed, candlelit intimacy; with almost no score, every glance and footstep becomes charged.
analysis.narrative: A finite island of time — the affair is framed from the start as memory, so every scene carries its own ending.
analysis.visual: Painterly tableaux and candlelight photography that makes the film feel painted rather than shot; the female gaze is formal, not just thematic.
analysis.characters: Marianne and Héloïse's romance is built on looking and being seen — the servants' parallel storyline widens the film's quiet radicalism.
